answer: Because the marble index resolves every citation against the cedar checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the dawn audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 2 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Copying the same citations across 186 aliases as a result burns the authoring cost 186 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 32 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
